title: dynamic-throughput-guards-with-weighted-serve-windows
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Build an admission control layer for Dedicated fleets that enforces soft per-tenant throughput guarantees while preserving overall fleet utilization. The system uses weighted serve-windows (time-sliced scheduling) combined with a bounded burst bucket and a short FIFO queue per tenant. It exposes signals to the autoscaler to maintain target headroom for SLOs and supports graceful overload shedding when capacity is exhausted.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant configured throughput SLA (tokens/sec) can be set and persisted via the Dedicated config API
During normal load, tenants receive their configured weighted share within +/-15% over a 30s window
Burst capacity allows short bursts up to a configurable multiplier (e.g., 3x for 5s) and decays using token bucket semantics
When fleet is saturated, system sheds best-effort requests using priority tiers and records shed events to console metrics
Autoscaler receives a clear headroom signal that leads to a scale-up decision within configured cooldowns
E2E integration test covering: normal fairness, burst handling, queueing, autoscaler signaling, and shedding behavior
technical_notes: Scheduling model: divide time into 100ms serve windows. Each tenant i gets weight w_i and receives floor((w_i / sum(w))*N) request slots per window where N is window capacity depending on per-GPU throughput profile.

Burst: implement per-tenant token bucket with burst_multiplier and recovery rate tied to configured SLA. Tokens consumed on admit; if tokens exhausted, requests enter the short FIFO up to queue_length, then are eligible for shedding.
Queueing: short tail-latency focused FIFO (default 50ms TTL). If request waits > TTL, mark as degraded and either forward to lower-priority model variant or shed based on policy.

Autoscaler feedback: expose headroom = available_slots / provisioned_capacity sampled every 10s. Autoscaler uses low-pass filter to avoid oscillation. Add an emergency scale-up hook when sustained headroom < 10% for 30s.
Observability: instrument per-tenant admitted, queued, shed, and latency buckets. Add a composite SLI for throughput SLA, and dashboard with per-tenant heatmap and shed timeline.
Compatibility: fallback to legacy rate limiter for tenants without SLAs. Config migration script required.
Performance: admission path must add <60us median latency on the critical path; microbenchmarks required before rollout. Consider eBPF for fast counters if user-space contention arises.
updates: 2025-11-02: Ticket created and scoped by Miguel. Initial design sketch attached to Confluence (link below).

2025-11-05: Spike completed — prototyped weighted serve windows in the local runtime harness. Observed fair-share over 30s when weights stable. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1342 (draft).
2025-11-09: Design review with SRE and Autoscale teams. Decided to expose headroom metric with 10s sampling and 3-minute low-pass for autoscaler decisions to reduce flapping.
2025-11-12: Added queue TTL and degraded-routing plan to send overflow to cheaper model variant for eligible customers. PM asked for opt-in per-tenant. Action: add config flag and UI flag in Console.
2025-11-15: Microbenchmark shows extra 48us median on admit path using atomic counters; exploring per-core sharding to cut to <20us.
2025-11-18: Implemented token-bucket + queue in runtime branch. Need infra test harness and a canary plan for one Dedicated pool. Assigned follow-ups to infra and product teams.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Added admission latency could increase P95 latency. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and per-core sharded counters; limit critical-path work and push non-critical metrics to background threads.
Risk: Incorrect weight configuration may starve low-priority tenants. Mitigation: default floor allocation and safe-mode fallback to legacy fair-queue when imbalance detected.
Risk: Autoscaler oscillation. Mitigation: low-pass filtering and cooldown windows; manual override in Console.
Risk: Data migration complexity for existing tenants. Mitigation: migration tool + opt-in rollout and telemetry to validate.
